title: Calibrate lexical-diversity bands on Old Czech letter-words controls
statement: The four planned clean and 2%-noise checks on C-059 cover a cipher family absent from the seven-family corpus registration. At seed 0, the known clean key compresses by 9.177% and misses criterion b only because its mean type-to-token ratio is 0.5955, above the calibrated 0.5913 limit. The fitted key reads 5,425 of 5,440 tokens exactly and encounters the same gate. At seed 1 the known and fitted keys pass the three core checks clean and noisy, with fitted savings 8.187% and 5.014%. Across diagnostic seeds 0 through 7 on the same clean source, the known key exceeds the upper type-to-token band at seeds 0, 4 and 6. The oracle calculation agrees with the complete evaluations at seeds 0 and 1. The standard noisy seed-0 fitted key passes the core checks at +5.703% compression savings and reads 5,262 of 5,440 tokens exactly. Its hapax share of 0.6700 exceeds the illusion-gate upper band of 0.6563. The noisy known key also exceeds that band.
check: Freeze disjoint calibration and control passages, plus held-out control seeds and layout sizes, before comparing the current per-chunk band to a candidate band calibrated on whole matched-size samples. Show true-key and fitted-key results for 0% and 2% noise on C-059, and check the same procedure on the already powered Czech and Middle English controls and the unchanged stock decoys. Report misses separately for compression, entropy, coverage, type-to-token ratio and illusion checks. Keep threshold choice independent of any manuscript score, report uncertainty over passages as well as cipher seeds, and review any scorer change before using it in a grid verdict. Check the hapax band in the illusion test separately from the reading test's type-to-token band.
